digest.component_or_area: test harness – nested pytest subprocess isolation
propositions: Nested pytest child subprocess omits --basetemp argument and joins user-global numbered temp root, causing pytest session-finish cleanup to synchronously scan and delete stale entries that can exceed the 90-second child timeout after test completion reports 100%.

Controlled filesystem A/B test with 400,000 stale entries proves the root cause: shared-root child took 10.8s for cleanup vs private-basetemp child took 0.882s, establishing cleanup cost scales with retained entries.

Nested pytest child should receive a caller-owned private basetemp (tmp_path/nested-pytest) via --basetemp to isolate session-finish cleanup while preserving ambient tracker HEAD/directories and store assertions.
Regression test confirms the fix: omitting --basetemp allows nested pytest to delete another run's sentinel file (RED), adding --basetemp preserves it (GREEN), and omitting again reproduces RED.
Stress test of 25 consecutive nested-pytest runs with private basetemp completed without timeout while a poisoned 200,000-entry shared root remained unchanged.
